title: Verifier‑Augmented LLM for Intent→Configuration Safety (Repaired Preregistration)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired study to test whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven intent→vendor-CLI configuration loop (generate→verify→repair, ≤2 repairs) reduces verifier-failure rates versus an LLM-only single-pass baseline on a synthetic NetOps task suite. The frozen confirmatory estimand was the per-task proportion of final verifier-pass within the repair budget. In a scientific pilot run (execution mode: scientific_pilot) we obtained 50 complete paired task outcomes. Both pipelines produced verifier-pass on all 50 paired tasks (baseline = 50/50, guarded = 50/50). Paired McNemar test p = 1.0; observed risk difference = 0.0 (95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). These pilot results do not support a measurable advantage for the verifier-augmentation under the executed conditions; the run was underpowered relative to the N=300 preregistered confirmatory plan and should be interpreted as a pilot providing procedural, artifact, and traceable-execution evidence rather than a definitive efficacy result.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent-based network configuration but raise safety and correctness concerns when outputs are applied. We preregistered a paired confirmatory study to evaluate whether integrating a deterministic verifier in a generate→verify→repair loop reduces configurations that fail deterministic validation compared with an LLM-only baseline. The final research question: Does verifier-augmentation produce a ≥30% relative reduction in verifier-failure proportion versus LLM-only within the prespecified repair budget?
sections.related_work: Key prior work motivating the study includes literature on automatic configuration repair and generate–validate–repair architectures (Liu et al., "Automatic Configuration Repair"), retrieval- and tool-augmented LLMs and RAG surveys, and intent→configuration translation research in NetOps (selected leads used in the preregistration). All cited sources are verified and recorded in the preregistration evidence list.
sections.methodology: We froze a machine-readable preregistration (study_id cand-427a). Confirmatory design: paired within-task comparison on intent→configuration synthesis. Planned N=300 tasks (10 synthetic topologies × 30 intents × 3 vendor CLIs), repair budget ≤2 LLM repair iterations per task, paired McNemar primary test (α=0.05). Synthetic tasks, three vendor-CLI families (Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, Arista EOS templates), deterministic verifier and reachability simulator used for pass/fail labels. Execution followed the preregistration retry, timeout, and exclusion rules. All prompts, model outputs, verifier logs, seeds, and artifact hashes are preserved (see execution_manifest and artifact hash list). The actual run executed as a scientific pilot: completed paired outcomes = 50 (complete_pair_count=50), model_calls_used=50, execution_mode=scientific_pilot.
sections.results: Confirmatory (pre-registered): complete paired count = 50. Baseline verifier-pass = 50/50 (1.0); Guarded (verifier-augmented) verifier-pass = 50/50 (1.0). Contingency: n11=50, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Observed risk difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729). Secondary/Exploratory: no discordant pairs occurred, so no within-run repair-iteration distribution or failure-mode breakdown was produced. Missingness/exclusions: none in the 50 completed pairs. All raw per-task artifacts and scoring JSON files are archived (paths and hashes recorded in execution_manifest).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: in this pilot, both pipelines produced verifier-pass on all executed tasks; therefore no evidence of improvement by the verifier-augmentation was observed. However, the run was a pilot (complete_pairs=50) versus the preregistered N=300; the absence of discordant outcomes prevents estimation of effect direction or repair-iteration behaviour. The result should be treated as an execution and artifact validation of the preregistered pipeline rather than a definitive test of the preregistered H1. Threats to validity include underpowered sample size relative to the preregistered plan, use of synthetic tasks and templates (construct and external validity limits), potential verifier completeness limitations, and dependence on a hosted LLM API (training-data contamination risk acknowledged and logged).
sections.conclusion: We completed an autonomous, preregistered pilot execution of a paired evaluator comparing an LLM-only pipeline to a verifier-augmented pipeline for intent→configuration synthesis. Both pipelines passed the deterministic verifier on all 50 paired pilot tasks (no observed difference). The pilot demonstrates reproducible artifact capture and an executable preregistered pipeline; larger confirmatory runs (per the preregistered N=300) are required before drawing efficacy conclusions about verifier-augmentation.

limitations: Underpowered pilot: the preregistration specified N=300 confirmatory tasks; the executed scientific_pilot produced 50 complete paired tasks, limiting confirmatory power and precluding reliable effect-size estimation.
Synthetic tasks and vendor templates: tasks used synthetic topologies and templated vendor CLIs (construct validity and external validity to real-world NetOps environments are limited).

Verifier scope and completeness: deterministic verifier correctness and coverage constrain what 'pass' means; verifier incompleteness or differing verifier semantics could mask operationally relevant failures.

Hosted LLM opacity and contamination risk: the hosted LLM API model identifier is recorded immutably in the archived execution/model_configuration.json, but model training data and internal behavior are opaque; possible training-data leakage or memorized canonical configs cannot be ruled out and were audited and logged where detected.

Pilot-only findings: absence of discordant pairs in this pilot prevents analysis of repair-iteration distributions, typical repair counts, and remaining failure-assertion categories; those exploratory questions remain unaddressed until a larger confirmatory run.

Reproducibility dependencies: reproduction requires access to the same hosted LLM (identifier in archived artifact), verifier implementation, and the execution artifacts; differences in provider behaviour or verifier versions can change outcomes.
